text:
sam_harrison: Hey team — Acme sent a bunch of failures on the embeddings endpoint after we rolled the batching change at 09:12 UTC. They see a mix of successful responses and 400s with dimension errors. Posting the raw error: 

sam_harrison: ```
ERROR [embed_route] requestId=acme-req-9876 status=400 msg="dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536"
payload={"model":"embed-large-v1","input_count":12,"batch_id":42}
```

maria_support: ack. Do we have the request payload from the customer? Any client-side change? Also is this single model or multiple variants?

sam_harrison: I asked for a repro but they included this sample call: 

sam_harrison: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["q1","q2",...],"batching":true}'
```

kevin_ml: @maria_support @sam_harrison thanks. That error strongly indicates that responses in a single batched RPC are coming from mismatched model instances or post-processing expecting different dim. Two likely classes: (1) model variant rotate (e.g., embed-large-v1 vs embed-large-quant) returning different dims, or (2) our batching aggregator applied an old/incorrect projection.

rebecca_obs: Can we get a per-request trace for one failing request? Looking for trace spans: accept->route->batcher->model->postprocess. Need the trace id or a request id. If logs have requestId=acme-req-9876 that's a good starting point. I'll instrument route-level latency breakdown and batch composition.

sam_harrison: attaching more logs from customer with request ids: acme-req-9876, acme-req-9877, acme-req-9889. They say failures are ~15% of requests during a 3m window.

infra-bot: deploy.bot: rollout embed-batcher v2 -> instances(12) started at 2026-03-11T09:11:45Z. Health checks OK. Canary traffic 10% -> 100% at 09:12:30Z.

kevin_ml: that aligns — v2 changed how we pad/concat tensors before projection to reduce copy. I suspect a race where a leftover KV cache or buffer from previous model variant (1536) gets mixed. Need batch-level metadata logs (model_checksum / variant_id) for each span. Can we enable debug sampling for the embed route?

maria_support: I can ask Acme for a raw failing response body. Meanwhile, @rebecca_obs can you pull the batch composition logs and the batcher debug traces for that 09:11–09:15 window? Also check if any model restarts coincide with those requestIds.

rebecca_obs: On it. Pulling traces now. Found trace acme-req-9876 -> trace_id=tr-0001. Batch composition: batch_id=42 included 12 entries: [req 9869..9880]. Spans show model_instance=embed-large-v1@node-7 for most, but two spans have model_instance=embed-large-quant@node-3 (quantized variant, 1536 dim). That's the smoking gun.

kevin_ml: aha. So a mixed-model batch. The inference worker should route homogeneous variants into same batch; v2 changed routing rules and apparently allowed cross-variant batching for throughput. We never expected different output dims. Immediate mitigation: revert v2 routing change or enforce variant-hash in batch key.

maria_support: Customer is asking for root cause and ETA for fix. Can we propose a quick mitigation (config flip) and a permanent fix timeline?

kevin_ml: Mitigation options: 
- Flip rollout to 10% canary (fast rollback) -> revert full traffic. 
- Add guard in batcher to include variant_id in batch key (fast patch, low risk). 
I'd push the guard as hotfix (30–90m) and rollback if needed.

rebecca_obs: I can add an alert that detects mixed-variant batches and rate of dimension-mismatch 400s. Also opening a dashboard panel: Embedding route -> Batch variant spread and 400 dimension errors by variant. Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/r/obs/embed-batch-variants (short-lived link).

sam_harrison: Doing customer comms now: told them we're investigating and will apply a mitigant. They asked whether this could cause billing anomalies — some responses succeeded and some failed — will partial billing show up?

maria_support: Good point. If we return 400 before a token is emitted we shouldn't bill, but if our gateway billed per-request acceptance that could cause discrepancy. Finance-team typically reconciles failed requests not billed, but need to confirm. @kevin_ml any chance batching caused double-charge?

kevin_ml: Unlikely. Billing occurs at acceptance in the front gate. Failures downstream lead to non-bill events by design. But I'll confirm with billing infra.

rebecca_obs: For observability postmortem: collect a sample of batch logs showing "batch_key" and "variant_id" fields, and attach the trace timelines showing model_instance per span. Also add per-request latency breakdown: batch_queue_time, model_inference_time, postprocess_time — we should surface percentiles.

maria_support: Action items summary (so we can send customer):
- Hotfix: enforce variant_id in batch key (kevin) — target 45m.
- Instrumentation: add mixed-variant alert and dashboard panel (rebecca) — target 1h.
- Confirm billing impact (maria + billing infra) — target 2h.
- Customer repro + logs (sam) — ongoing.

kevin_ml: I'll open PR for guard and request an expedited review. If guard is risky, we'll rollback batcher v2 to previous release (infra will handle).

infra-bot: deploy.bot: rollback embed-batcher v2 -> starting rollback at 2026-03-11T10:02:15Z (triggered by kevin_ml).

sam_harrison: customer update sent: "we identified a mixed-model batching issue introduced in the recent batcher rollout. We're rolling back the change and pushing a guard. We'll follow up with more details and a patch ETA." They replied :thumbsup: and asked for trace ids for their team — I provided tr-0001/tr-0002.

rebecca_obs: Follow-ups: add unit test to ensure batch key includes variant_id, and add a small e2e that simulates two model variants and asserts no mixing occurs. I'll add dashboards with per-request latency breakdown panel and link in the thread.

maria_support: Logging notes for the postmortem: ensure the error includes the expected_dim and actual_dim and model_variant identifiers so customers get actionable info.

kevin_ml: Thanks all. After rollback I'll run a canary with the guard in place in a staging cluster, then promote. I'll post PR and staging run logs here.

infra-bot: monitoring.bot: anomaly detected: embed 400-dim-errors spike -> 14% between 09:10–09:16 UTC, returned to baseline after rollback at 10:02 UTC.

sam_harrison: closing loop with customer — they asked to be notified when fix is live. I set a watch and will DM when rollout complete.

maria_support: closing tasks for now; will open a postmortem doc after we've gathered artifacts. :white_check_mark:
